nom: The Ordinary Amino Acids + B5 Hydration Serum

segments.dry: Dry-skin reviewers form the largest group and mostly report strong, lasting hydration and relief from flaking, tightness, and chapped patches, including several using the serum alongside tretinoin or other drying actives.
segments.oily: Reviewers with oily skin have mixed results: one says the watery serum does nothing for her and prefers a heavier product, while others with oily-to-combination skin report it hydrates without adding grease.
segments.combination: Combination-skin reviewers, including several who also describe dry or sensitive patches, generally report good hydration without clogged pores, though one reports breakouts after adding it to her routine.
segments.sensitive: Sensitive-skin reviewers, including some with rosacea or eczema, mostly report no irritation and good tolerance, though a few note stinging or dilute the serum to make it more comfortable.
segments.mature: A few reviewers in their late 40s to 50s describe the serum as a staple for mature or aging skin, reporting firmer, smoother skin and softer fine lines with regular use.

concerns.dehydration: Hydration is the serum's most consistently reported effect: reviewers across skin types describe it as one of the most hydrating products they've used, often replacing a moisturizer or hyaluronic acid that didn't work for them, though a couple of reviewers still felt dry after months of use.
concerns.blemishes: Reports on breakouts are sharply divided: a notable group describes new or worsened breakouts, milia, or aggravated sebaceous filaments after starting the serum, while a separate, larger group reports no breakouts at all or even a reduction in existing acne and barrier-damage breakouts.
concerns.barrier: Several reviewers credit the serum with repairing a damaged moisture barrier after over-exfoliation or harsh actives, describing restored comfort and reduced sensitivity over weeks of use.
concerns.redness: A handful of reviewers report the serum calmed redness and irritation, including alongside contact dermatitis and general redness-prone skin.
concerns.aging: A few reviewers mention softer fine lines or firmer-looking skin alongside the serum's hydrating effect, though this is a secondary observation rather than the product's main reported benefit.

aspects.libelle: Sticky or tacky finish when applied to dry skin
Feels less sticky when applied to damp skin
Dropper bottle spills or is hard to control
Small bottle empties quickly given how often it's used

extraits.texte: I am so so upset that this has caused me to breakout so badly, even when I was having pimples it was never like this and some are so sore. I will be travelling next week and wanted to make my skin nice and now I have just made it worse… I understand everyone has a different reaction but mine was definitely not good and I am so upset

This product really does what it claims to do, i.e. hydration. HOWEVER, it saddens me to say that I just found out that it's the culprit for the white, sebaceous threads protruding out of my skin - especially in my T-zone and chin area. It unfortunately aggravates my sebaceous filaments. And it's really bad....I have dark skin, so having 'white hairy-like threads' all over my face isn't pretty. I've had to really up my exfoliating game because of the product. As much as I love TO's hydrators, I think they may be too concentrated. Perhaps, having an option for a diluted version would be more suited for some of us.

extraits.titre: Still on the fence about this product!
extraits.texte: I have to give 3 stars to this product because, after using all the content of the bottle over the course of various months, I am still confused about whether I actually liked it or not. For a bit of context: I have dry skin, which can really only take as much in terms of the amount of products I layer, and of how thick they are; I initially bought this serum in the hopes of it providing an extra layer of hydration under my moisturiser. The aim was to avoid embarking on the never-ending quest for a light-yet-effective moisturiser that my skin could handle, so I thought this water-based would do the trick of provding extra moisture without any added heaviness. It initially caused breakouts, but they eventually faded after a few days of consistent use. So far so good. BUT what never really changed over the course of time was the sticky finish that it left my skin covered in (which I really didn't look forward to, considering that I bought it very much to avoid this thing, which also tends to happen with thicker moisturisers). Nothing I did ever really managed to solve this problem (I tried applying less of it, layering it with less products, using it by itself, applying it on damp skin to improve absorption). On this note, I very much agree with some reviews I read that claimed it left a sticky film on the skin, which resembles very much what you would be left with if you were to apply fruit juice or sugary water on your skin and let it dry. Of all the many serums I have tried from the Ordinary, and any other skincare line, this is without a doubt my favorite. I buy it again and again. I would say the best way to describe the effect this has on my fair, dry, sensitive skin is: strength. My skin feels protected, firm, bouncy, and strong after I use it. It is light and feels like a deep drink of water. When I ruined my skin barrier a few years ago I broke out in acne and dry skin patches. This serum helped restore my skin barrier and clear my skin. I'm 29. I have been using this for about 4 years. I wear it morning and night under my moisturizers. It will continue to be a staple of my routine indefinitely.

I bought this product as a light, water based hydration booster for my face but ended up loving it so much that I ordered 3 more bottles. Not only that it is so light and fresh on the skin (have no idea why other people are mentioning sticky finish) but it also drastically improved contact dermatitis on my fingers. Pro tip: I use it on wet hair to hydrate the ends and it makes it slightly more flexible and easier to brush. I am a female with oily to combination skin, 34 yo with rather sensitive, rosy skin.

I didn't expect to like this so much but wanted to try a few different things for my severely dry skin that just can't hold onto moisture. At first I was disappointed because my skin didn't feel that juicy nourished plumpness you get from a lot of hydrating serums, but at the end of the day I realized my skin was STILL soft. It feels like this actually repairs the moisture barrier instead of just temporarily infusing it with moisture, so my skin feels firm and healthy. After continual use for a couple weeks, my skin actually feels healthier, even when I haven't just put it on. It also delivers quite a "shine" (even though it is NOT greasy at all) which may be too much for oilier skin types. For dry skin, I love this more than any hyaluronic acid or the Buffet!

If you have redness and dry skin, this will be your best friend. This works wonders for my dry skin and calms my redness all Day! The hydration is INCREDIBLE more than any hylaronic acid could ever do for me
